clue.text: Rawness can produce wrong ones

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of rawness are put out of order and set right again

explanation.surface: A green, inexperienced candidate is likely to get things wrong in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' tells you to rearrange RAWNESS; the whole clue then describes what a raw beginner gives in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexperience leads to incorrect replies, so the whole sentence describes mistaken responses.

clue.text: Declared a supporter in a possible deal

indicators.note: in places the supporter inside the rearranged letters of deal
possible suggests one possible arrangement of the letters of deal

parts.note: a leg is something that supports, like a table leg

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have backing for a potential business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' signals an anagram of deal, giving ALED; 'supporter' as a leg is the misdirection, since it reads as a backer of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alleged has been asserted or stated, usually without proof yet, so it has been declared.

clue.text: Spit in the sea

parts.note: reads like rudely spitting into the water, but a spit is a narrow ridge of sand jutting into the water

explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a long sandy ridge, a natural shoal that rises from shallow coastal water.

clue.text: Run out of pictures to put up

parts.note: ex is a Latin prefix meaning out of or from

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the letters are written upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pictures as a body of work are art

explanation.surface: Someone has run short of paintings to hang on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put up' makes ART read upwards as TRA. In cricket a run scored not off the bat, such as a wide, is called an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an extra is a run conceded through a bye, wide or no-ball rather than hit.

clue.text: At sea, curses tea clippers

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors swear as tea is carried on fast sailing ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' signals rearranging CURSESTEA. Tea clippers were fast nineteenth-century cargo ships, which gives the nautical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are garden shears used for clipping and pruning plants, so they are clippers.

clue.text: Perfectionist has trouble with saucepan

parts.note: to make a fuss is to cause trouble or bother
a saucepan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: A fastidious cook is struggling with a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is a person who is overly particular about details, much like a perfectionist.

clue.text: The one opposite appears to look right

parts.note: to face is to look towards something

explanation.surface: A person seated across from you seems to be glancing to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A facer is literally one who faces, so it is the person positioned opposite you.

clue.text: Astounded -not all at the same time

definitions.meaning: ... as in amazed or bowled over

definitions.text: not all at the same time
definitions.meaning: ... as in arranged at intervals, like ... start times

explanation.surface: Someone was shocked to find things did not happen at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deeply shocked and spread out over intervals rather than simultaneous.

clue.text: French upstart

parts.note: a word borrowed from French for someone newly risen to wealth or status, literally one who has arrived

explanation.definitionFit: This loanword from French names a social climber who has suddenly become rich or important.

clue.text: They go round filling potholes

parts.note: suggests road menders, but means travelling menders who patch holes in pots and pans

explanation.definitionFit: Tinkers were itinerant menders of kettles and pots, travelling from door to door to fix holes.

clue.text: Involved in a cult that's crazy

indicators.note: involved means entangled or twisted up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Joining a cult is something only a madman would do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' tells you to rearrange the seven letters of IN A CULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means insane or wildly foolish, the same as crazy.

clue.text: Companion given a smile, despite one's annoyance

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A friend gets a smile from you even though you are irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyance, especially at being humiliated or disappointed.

clue.text: Tribal rag turns out to be rock

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tribal newspaper proves to be solid as stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' tells you to rearrange TRIBALRAG; 'rag' looks like a newspaper but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is famously known as the Rock, the limestone promontory at Spain's southern tip.

clue.text: Look back into the Middle Ages for capital savers

indicators.note: into places the reversed word inside the central letters
the Middle points to the central letters of the word Ages
back means the word for look is written backwards

parts.note: to look is to see

explanation.surface: Peer backwards into the medieval period for people who rescued the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives a reversal and 'the Middle' takes the central pair of letters from Ages. Cackling geese famously warned ancient Rome of an attack on the Capitol, hence capital savers.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says sacred cackling birds raised the alarm and saved Rome's Capitol from the Gauls.

clue.text: Game requiring many skills

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword sign for many
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: A sport that demands lots of ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing small missiles at a board, so it is a game.

clue.text: It smells awful when it goes off

definitions.text: It smells awful when it goes off

parts.words: It smells awful when it goes off
parts.note: reads like spoiled food going off, but means a prank device that releases a stench when set off

explanation.definitionFit: A stink bomb is a small capsule that releases a foul smell when broken or set off.

clue.text: They may give a lift to potential down-and-outs

definitions.text: They may give a lift to potential down-and-outs

parts.words: They may give a lift to potential down-and-outs
parts.note: sounds like charity for the homeless, but means upward punches to boxers who may be knocked down and out

explanation.definitionFit: Upward blows in boxing lift an opponent's chin and may lead to a knockout.

clue.text: Feed a pet sugar, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: You might give your dog something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of A PET SUGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is grazing land or grass eaten by livestock, so it is animal feed.

clue.text: Blooming good example of self-interest

parts.note: a flowering plant named after the youth of myth who fell in love with his own reflection

explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil genus is named after the vain youth who pined for his own reflection.

clue.text: It might be rash to touch them

definitions.text: It might be rash to touch them

parts.words: It might be rash to touch them
parts.note: rash seems to mean reckless, but means a skin rash from stinging plants

explanation.definitionFit: Stinging plants with irritating hairs bring up an itchy skin rash when brushed against.

clue.text: Understand and cash in

definitions.meaning: to grasp or become aware of it
to ... an asset is to convert it into money

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the situation and sells up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to become aware of something and to convert assets into money.

clue.text: Put off Edward's return with hesitation

indicators.note: return means the name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Edward hesitates about coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' signals a reversal; Edward's short form is a crossword staple, and 'Put off' reads like postponing rather than discouraging.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or dissuade someone, so it means put off.

clue.text: Got up immediately after a meal, making a bloomer

indicators.note: immediately after puts the word for got up straight after the meal

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up from the table straight after eating and makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a garden flower, and anything that blooms can be called a bloomer.

clue.text: The only thing a defeated army can beat

definitions.text: The only thing a defeated army can beat

parts.words: The only thing a defeated army can beat
parts.note: beat seems to mean defeat, but refers to the phrase beat a hasty withdrawal

explanation.definitionFit: A beaten army can only beat a withdrawal, the idiom being to beat a hasty one.

clue.text: Trail used by a tank

definitions.meaning: a tank moves on caterpillar treads

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rough path and the continuous tread a tank runs on.

clue.text: Coarse actors are plastered

parts.note: rough means coarse
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Crude performers have been drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' suggests drunk but means coated with a rendering of lime and gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: To roughcast a wall is to coat it with coarse plaster, so roughcast means plastered.

clue.text: Note on qualified dockyard job

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
fit means qualified or suitable

explanation.surface: A memo about a competent worker in the shipyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is the overhaul and re-equipping of a ship in dock.

clue.text: The warmth gets right into the centre

indicators.note: into puts the letter for right inside the word for warmth

parts.note: heat means warmth

explanation.surface: Warmth spreads correctly through the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its core or middle, as in the heart of the city.

clue.text: Stopped working

parts.note: can mean broke down, but here means made redundant from a job, or ceased doing something

explanation.definitionFit: Workers who are laid off have been dismissed, so they are no longer employed.

clue.text: A big hit, poetry that is fashionable

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A huge success, that poem is in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in the current fashion, so it means fashionable.

clue.text: Ready to accept simple drink

indicators.note: to accept means the word for ready takes the herb inside it

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
a simple is an old name for a medicinal herb

explanation.surface: A person keen to take something plain to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' is an old noun for a medicinal plant, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sweet fizzy drink or fruit cordial, so it is a beverage.

clue.text: Beg for something nice to follow in French

indicators.note: to follow puts the nice thing after the French word

parts.note: en is the French for in
a treat is something pleasant

explanation.surface: Ask for a dessert to come next, speaking French.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or ask earnestly, the same as beg.
